summary: Malheur NF platform and firefinder stand from the 1930s, used into the 1960s; tent cabin gone, platform and stand still there on 2022 visits.

facts.design: Wooden platform with a firefinder stand; a tent cabin or tent camp nearby, now gone
facts.status_note: Tent cabin gone. The wooden platform and firefinder stand remained on 2022 visits.

access.note: On Malheur National Forest land, reached by Forest Service roads. One 2022 report says a road is closed in hunting season; no closure notice for the site found.

visit.trail_note: Walk from the road's end: a few hundred feet by one 2022 visitor, about a mile and a half by another

events.note: Lookout site 'starting in 1930' (cherylhill.net); FFLOS says 1930s. Platform with firefinder stand and tent camp; no cabin or tower built.

evidence.supports: built in the 1930s as a platform with a firefinder stand and tent cabin
evidence.quote: Built in the 1930s as a platform with a firefinder stand and tent cabin.

evidence.supports: tent cabin gone; platform and firefinder stand remain as of 2022
evidence.quote: The tent cabin is gone, but the platform and stand for the firefinder remain as of 2022.

evidence.supports: about 28 miles southeast of John Day
gone cabin, wooden platform still there (firelookout.com)

evidence.quote: Crane Point was a lookout site starting in 1930.

evidence.supports: platform with fire finder stand and tent camp; no cabin or tower
evidence.quote: No cabin or tower was built here, just a platform with fire finder stand on the summit and a nearby tent camp

evidence.supports: everything gone except weathered fire finder stand and old platform (2022 visit)
evidence.quote: Everything is gone now except for the weathered fire finder stand and the old platform.

evidence.quote: The platform used for Crane Point is still there along with the stand for the fire finder.

evidence.supports: platform in decent condition minus a few rotting boards
evidence.quote: The platform itself was still in decent condition minus a few boards that had signs of rot.

corrections.why: The register says the wooden platform and firefinder stand remained as of 2022, and two 2022 visit reports found them there. Only the tent cabin is gone. Human review: 'ruins' is the closest value for a platform and stand without a cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: cherylhill.net says the site was a lookout starting in 1930; the register says the 1930s. Both fit a 1930s start; the record has no built year, and the event above uses 1930 from cherylhill.net.

sources.title: Crane Point - Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Two independent 2022 visit reports agree the platform and stand remain. The brief's conflict note says firelookout.com is 'standing'; its page reads 'Gone. Wooden platform still there.' for the cabin and platform, so the note is slightly off. Built year: 1930 (cherylhill.net) vs 1930s (FFLOS, firelookout.com); the record has no built year. Staff: none named in sources. Photos on FFLOS and firelookout.com are courtesy credits with no licence; none added. Road closure in hunting season is a seasonal restriction on one road, not the site.
